title: {name} for families
description: A profile for each child, set by a parent: what is explained at their age, a lock under 13, and a notice if something serious comes up, without reading their messages. No account for your child, free and open source.
h1: AI for your children, set by you.
lede: Each child gets a profile of their own. You choose what is explained to them for their age, under 13 it opens only with you, and if something serious comes up, you’re told, without reading their messages.

decide.title: A profile for each child, set by you.
decide.why: You know better than anyone what your child is ready to hear, and when.
decide.more: And six more topics, each with the same three choices.
decide.list: Nine sensitive topics, each with three answers: explain it for their age, talk with you first, or later, saying why.
Vikidia, the encyclopedia for 8 to 13-year-olds, or Wikipedia.
The AI that answers them, chosen by you.
Nothing changes without your password or passkey.
told.title: Told, without reading their diary.
told.why: A child who knows everything is read stops confiding. {name} tells you that a concern came up, not what they wrote.
told.list: Four kinds of concern: self-harm or suicide; abuse or violence; an adult asking for secrecy, pictures or a meeting; bullying or threats.
You see its kind and the time, never their words.
If the danger is at home, you aren’t told: {name} gives your child a helpline and urges them to talk to another trusted adult.
Your child knows this from the first day.
Time spent, today and over seven days.
{name} spots a concern a little more than half the time across languages; the AI that answers can raise one too.
told.source: 85% of parents want to be alerted if their child discusses something harmful. National Parents Union, 2026
sees.title: What your child sees.
sees.why: A profile of their own: their conversations, their memory, their files. Nothing crosses between profiles.
sees.answer: Picture a pizza cut into 4 equal slices. Eat 1 and you’ve eaten 1 slice out of 4: we write it 1/4. The bottom number says how many slices there are, the top one how many you take. Shall we try with a bar of chocolate?
sees.list: No account, no email address: their profile lives on your computer.
Under 13 it opens with you; from the school year they turn 13, alone, or with their own lock.
They see what was chosen for them: “{tier}”.
Their conversations stay theirs, unless they share one with you.
learn.title: Learning, not copying. Measured before it’s promised.
learn.why: An AI that hands out answers lifts practice scores, then exam scores fall. One that guides doesn’t.
learn.body: In a child’s profile, every message goes with instructions to help them understand rather than do the work for them. We measure, AI by AI and in four languages, how often it gives the answer anyway. We’ll call it a tutor only when that’s rare.

where.title: At home, not with us.
where.why: There is no {name} server. What {name} keeps stays encrypted on your computer. What changes is the AI that answers.
where.cards: The private AI, downloaded once (3.1 GB). Nothing leaves, even offline. It needs 12 GB of memory and a recent graphics chip.
A plan or a key of yours, if its terms allow your child’s age. Their messages then go to that provider.
“{free}” isn’t offered in a child’s profile: that service is for people over 18.
family.title: And for the whole family.
limits.title: What {name} doesn’t do.
limits.items: Keep your child from opening another AI or app: your device’s parental controls do that.
Promise the rule always holds: smaller AIs keep it less well, which is why we measure.
Catch every concern: it misses some, and flags some that aren’t.
Alert you on your phone: the notice shows on this computer.
Work everywhere without a plan: the private AI needs a recent computer.
Replace a teacher, a doctor, or you.
faq.title: Your questions.
faq.items: Is it a ChatGPT for kids?
It’s an AI of the same kind, in a browser tab, with a profile for each child that you set. The AI that answers is the one on this computer, or your own.
You enter their year of birth. Under 13, their profile opens only with you; from the school year they turn 13, they open it alone.
No, neither you nor your child. Everything is on your computer.
{name} is free and open source, for as many children as you like. So is the private AI; a plan for an AI is paid to its provider.
No. You see the time spent, and a concern if one comes up. Their conversations stay theirs, unless they share one.
Their profile asks the AI to help them understand rather than do it for them. We measure how often it does anyway, and publish it.
In a recent browser, on the family computer, a tablet or a phone. Nothing to install.
A profile each, on the same computer, at no extra cost. Nothing crosses from one to another.
start.title: Three steps, on your computer.
start.steps: Enter their year of birth, then choose, topic by topic.
start.note: Opens {name} on a new profile, your choices first. Nothing to install.
